rationale:
Rung 2, and this is the batch that closes a spine the loop has been building since #12.

The diagnosis first, because the important finding this pass is about the loop and not the town. Three consecutive workers — #17, #19, #20 — each opened with context-budget printing OVER, each wrote a cue saying so, and each made it worse. c38, c42 and #20's closing cue are the same cue reported three times. Individually every one of those workers was right and did the correct thing; collectively they produced three identical observations and no fix, because the file they were reporting on is mine and none of them could touch it. That is precisely the shape that killed Solvista — nine iterations independently concluding the same true thing — arriving eighteen iterations earlier and in a smaller register. So curation came before planning this pass, and it was done structurally.

The budget was 52.0 KB against a 46 KB cap and is now 43.3. The ledger had never been rotated: 13 entries, 75 KB. But rotation alone would not have helped, because a worker reads the last THREE entries and those three had grown to 15.3 KB by themselves — #19's entry alone is 6.5 KB. Entry length is charged three times over, and nothing capped it. So: rotated to 8, then appended the full text of #18-#20 verbatim to LEDGER-archive.md and condensed what stays in LEDGER.md (15.3 -> 9.1 KB, nothing lost), and put a ~3.5 KB per-entry cap into the ledger's own template with the reason written next to it, so the next worker is told where the excess belongs — a law goes to LAWS.md, a loose end goes to state.json, and neither belongs in a longer entry. state.json's inventory had drifted back into implementation histories for the third time (the `life` entry was 2.9 KB of prose about how yearBusy was built) and is back to nouns; cues went 19 -> 5. LAWS.md I let reach 11.4/12 KB while promoting from #18-#20 and then cut back to 11.0, because the rule is that at the cap you cut to add: I dropped the ticker-queue law outright, since its content is now carried exactly by the inventory line describing the ticker, and compressed two anecdotes out of the probe laws. Four of the five promotions were merges into laws that already existed rather than new entries — #19's cap-floor lesson extends the time-compression law that already said caps set inflow, #18's discontinuity lesson extends the constant-to-variable law, #20's scatter lesson extends the 0.9-cells law. Only #19's flat-peak law is genuinely new. Net: 27 laws in, 27 out, sharper.

Now the town. The spine since pass #10 has been: the world got a year at #12, and a year nothing reads is a lighting change. Pass #15 counted three readers. There are now six — day length, light, the courtyard beds, all thirteen trees, the working day, the population caps — and exactly two systems are left running on a constant or a dead ramp. Those two are this batch's first and third briefs, and when they land the question 'should this read the year?' will have been asked everywhere it pays.

b20 is the batch's bet and it is the oldest debt on the board. `stepClouds()` decides every front in this town with `R() < 0.3 + 0.24 * richness()`, and the rain roll under it scales on `(0.6 + rich)`. `richness()` is `clamp(day/16, 0, 1)`: it pinned at 1 in real minute fifteen and has been a constant ever since. So the weather is not merely year-blind, it is driven by a variable that stopped varying — the same defect `maturity()` had, found at pass #10, spent everywhere except here. c25 has been the top cue since #10 and I have now declined it twice. It goes first. Folded into it: c8, because a rain roll gated on `daylight > 0.15` means a front peaking overnight builds full cover and can never rain, which in an 11.5-hour winter day would make the season b20 has just made cloudiest the season least able to rain — the bug and the feature are the same seam and splitting them would ship a contradiction. Also c35, because rain is this brief's own feature and `motion.mjs` cannot see a raindrop: they are screen-space and absent from `__entities()`. A brief whose gate cannot cover the thing it changed is a brief that ships on a screenshot.

b21 exists because b20 makes it matter. c7 has been open since #2 and has looked like polish every time I read it: the sun's disc is veiled by cloud but the ground was never told, so under 0.95 cover the sky is a grey lid and the lane below it is full of crisp midday shadows. It has been cheap-and-cosmetic for eighteen iterations. The moment b20 lands, heavy overcast stops being a rare event and becomes most of a winter, and the defect is on screen for a large share of the year. Ordering it second is the whole point of it.

b22 is the starved domain and the other half of the spine. River has had one iteration in twelve. It is also, I think, the most defensible 'this is the same in February and August' left in the town: `updateBoat` spawns at a flat `R() < dt*0.012`, always at y=-7 heading south at speed 1.05, and the water's flow is twelve anonymous streaks drawn inline in the frame loop at one speed and one colour — no function, no name. I have put that in the inventory so the worker has something to reach for. The explicit constraint is that winter must not be boatless: the boat is the town's only long-travelling object and `boatWatch()`, the domain's best behaviour, dies with it.

b23 is the one brief that is not about the year, and it is deliberate seed for the next pass. #20's closing cue found that `answersTouch()` answers everything except PATH — so the plaza roundel around the fountain and the entire courtyard path ring are dead to the cursor and the click, and `PAVING.plaza` has only ever fired on 24 cells of the world's 2,903 paved ones. The town advertised its clickability at #13 and then declined to answer on the surface an eye goes to first. It is also the reason I am not climbing this pass despite the spine closing: rung 5, change the observer, is where this loop should go next, and I would rather arrive there having just done one observer-side brief than from a cold start. If b20 through b24 land, pass #25 climbs to 5.

b24 is the tail and it is a measurement I am prepared to have come back empty. c30: the allotments inherit `bloomCap` through the shared `caTick` path, so nothing ripens in deep winter, `ripePlots()` goes to zero and the arrival source that reads it damps away for about a fifth of the year. That is seasonally correct and entirely unmeasured — nobody has checked the gardeners come back at the right rate in spring, or that seventeen plots of bare earth read as resting rather than as a system that has died. The brief says measure first and decide from the numbers, and says explicitly that 'measured, it is correct, here are the numbers' is an acceptable shipped outcome. I would rather buy that answer once than carry the cue for another ten passes.

Risk: one high, three medium, one low, and the low one is sequenced so it is not the comfortable option — it is the cleanup that the high-risk brief creates the need for.
